title: AuthorityMatrix
description: Authority matrix for repo separation, scoped admin rights, separation of duties and end-to-end closure (issue #150, EPIC-00 #144). A matrix declares the repos under governance, the principals (per-repo fleets plus exactly one enterprise controller) that may act on them, the actors inside each principal (each carrying a chain-of-command role, a persona posture and a model tier), and the work items whose closure is gated on recorded gate + `make verify` evidence. Document validity is NOT the same as closure: `gate_evidence`/`verify_evidence` are optional at the document level because their absence is a runtime closure denial (issue #150: 'a missing or empty evidence field is a denial, never a pass'), never a pass and never a document failure. Structurally malformed input (unparseable YAML, non-mapping root) is CANNOT-ASSESS; a violation of this schema or of a semantic invariant is a real defect (NOT-OK).

version.description: Matrix format version. The engine understands version 1 only; a version it does not understand is CANNOT-ASSESS (a matrix this engine cannot read is never a pass).

repos.description: Every repo under governance. A repo names the fleet that administers it; rights are per repo, so an undeclared repo has no authority record at all.

principals.description: The authority holders: one repo-fleet per repo plus exactly one enterprise-controller (semantic invariant 'cross-repo-single', enforced by the engine).

work_items.description: Work items under closure governance: each names its repo and its separation-of-duties assignment, and optionally carries the recorded evidence that would make it closed.

repoId.description: A repository in <owner>/<name> form, e.g. kushin77/agent-orchestrator.

action.description: The closed action vocabulary an admin right grants: 'files' (read/write the repo's files), 'issues' (create/edit/close its issues), 'state' (read/write its fleet state: claims, sessions, board), 'merge' (merge into its protected branch; additionally requires an actor with merge_authority), 'rollup' (cross-repo read/aggregation; inherently cross-repo, so only a cross_repo principal may hold it).

role.description: Chain-of-command role (harvested vocabulary: capital-underwriting docs/wiki/ELITE_*_CHARTER.md). The commander is the only role with merge authority and performs no execution; the lieutenant-commander is the execution arm; soldiers/snipes do bounded mechanical work; the auditor audits adversarially and never executes.

posture.description: Persona posture (closed platform vocabulary shared with registry/personas/persona-card.schema.json): 'executor' performs primary work, 'reviewer' independently reviews an executor's work, 'auditor' adversarially audits claims/evidence. A posture only ever fills the duty it names, and an auditor is never the executor of what it audits.

modelTier.description: Dispatch tier on the flash/pro ladder (registry/personas defaultModelTier vocabulary, docs/MODEL-PROFILES.md). Used by the tier-floor rule: the auditor of a work item must not be dispatched below its executor.

fleet.description: Id of the repo-fleet principal that administers this repo. The fleet's scope must be exactly this repo (semantic invariant 'fleet-scope-single').

gate.description: The repo's own make-verify command, recorded verbatim so closure evidence can be checked against the gate the repo actually publishes.

admin_rights.description: The rights this repo delegates to its fleet. The fleet's own admin_rights must be a subset (a fleet cannot self-grant more than the repo delegates).

actor.description: One identity inside a principal. Actors are the principals separation of duties reasons about: executor != reviewer != auditor for one work item, as three distinct actors.

merge_authority.description: True only for a commander actor (semantic invariant 'merge-authority-commander'). Absent means false.

principal.description: An authority holder. Exactly one principal in the matrix has cross_repo: true and it must be the enterprise-controller (semantic invariant 'cross-repo-single'): every other principal is confined to the repos in its scope.

kind.description: 'repo-fleet' is a repo's own engineering team with scoped admin rights; 'enterprise-controller' is the single cross-repo actor that rolls up across repos.

scope.description: The repos this principal may act on. A repo absent from every scope is actionable by nobody but the enterprise controller.

cross_repo.description: True for the enterprise controller only. A second cross_repo principal is a validation failure (NOT-OK), because it re-opens exactly the cross-repo hole the matrix exists to close.

evidence.description: A recorded gate result. The schema checks SHAPE only (each field, when present, has the right type): completeness and truthfulness are decided at closure time, not here, because issue #150 requires a missing or empty evidence field to be an explicit closure DENIAL rather than a document failure. An evidence record with an absent or whitespace-only output, a non-zero exit code, a commit that is not the item's head, a repo that is not the item's repo, or a recorder with no authority on that repo is a closure DENIAL.

repo.description: Repo the evidence was recorded in. Must equal the work item's repo (closure DENY otherwise).

output.description: The command's literal output. Recorded output is the only thing that makes evidence real — a claim of a result is not evidence.

git_sha.description: The commit under test; evidence always names a commit (parity with governance/merge: a green check that cannot name a commit cannot close work).

recorded_by.description: Actor id of the recorder. It must resolve to an actor whose principal is scoped to this repo.

sodAssignment.description: Separation-of-duties assignment for one work item: three distinct actor ids, each filling the duty its posture names. The keys are optional here because an unassigned duty is a separation DENIAL ('sod-duty-unassigned'), not a document failure.

head_sha.description: The commit under test. When declared, both evidence records must name it (closure evidence names a COMMIT).

gate_evidence.description: The fleet's own gate result for this item. Absent means 'not recorded', which is a closure denial.

verify_evidence.description: The repo-level `make verify` result for this item. Absent means 'not recorded', which is a closure denial.
